thread:
dave_customer: Hey team — since we flipped our on-prem egress to go through our colo transit, we've seen traffic to Redwood land in eu-west-1 instead of us-west-2. Huge latency, some 403s and token billing spike. Anyone seen this pattern?

alice_support: Sorry you're hit, Dave. Can you paste a minimal curl + response headers and a traceroute? Also which private egress (NAT IP) did you observe from your side? :eyes:

dave_customer: Repro steps: from an app host inside our VPC -> curl to Redwood API:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDBOX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (52.31.12.44) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< x-region: eu-west-1
< x-request-id: rq_abc123
```
Traceroute from host: 
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (52.31.12.44), 30 hops max
 1  10.1.0.1 (10.1.0.1)  0.3 ms  0.3 ms  0.3 ms
 2  192.0.2.5 (192.0.2.5)  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.0 ms
 3  198.51.100.9 (198.51.100.9)  12.1 ms  12.0 ms  12.3 ms
 4  * * *
 5  52.31.12.44 (52.31.12.44)  180.4 ms  179.9 ms  180.2 ms
```
Public egress IP seen by Redwood dashboard: 3.124.55.10 (that's our colo NAT in EU)

bob_neteng: That looks like SNAT at your transit/colo NAT is choosing the EU egress IP. Because the source IP is from 10.0/16 it gets SNAT'd to the transit NAT (3.124.55.10) which we see as EU and route to eu region endpoints. Likely causes: BGP local-preference on the transit, AWS TGW route table, or a proxy with region-biased egress.

alice_support: Can you confirm whether you recently changed any BGP announcements or if the transit provider adjusted next-hops? Also, do you have a forced proxy (squid/HAProxy) that SNATs to a colo IP?

dave_customer: We did push a route update to prefer the colo egress for cost reasons last week. I thought it would still pick us-west for Redwood because of geo-DNS. I can roll it back but want to understand if there's a smaller config to avoid auth/billing/latency issues.

carol_oncall: Note: when our edge sees requests from 3.124.55.10 we map to eu model pool by region header. That explains the 403 (token tied to us tenant/region) and higher latency. We should treat this as a customer-side egress misroute. Action items: 1) collect pcap at time of failure, 2) share sample x-request-id (rq_abc123), 3) check customer NAT IP mapping in our access logs, 4) provide recommended route/NAT config.

bob_neteng: Quick recommended mitigations:
- If you must egress via colo NAT, add a specific static route for Redwood IP blocks toward your US egress (avoid default 0.0.0.0/0 match).
- Disable source NAT on the colo proxy for traffic to api.redwood.ai (pass-through) so original source IPs are preserved and region selection can work.
- On BGP, increase local-pref for the US path for prefixes hosting api.redwood.ai.
- Short term: add a SNAT exception in your NAT device for 52.31.0.0/16 -> keep source IP or map to a US egress IP.

alice_support: Can you try one quick test, Dave? From the same host, force IPv4 source of a US egress by using `curl --interface <us-egress-ip>` (if available) or temporary iptables SNAT rule: `iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -d 52.31.0.0/16 -j SNAT --to-source X.Y.Z.W` and re-run the call. If that returns 200 and x-region: us-west-2 then it's confirmed.

dave_customer: Will try now. If confirmed we'll either add a static route for Redwood prefixes to go to our us NAT or add a NAT exception.

infra-bot: New support ticket created: SUP-2026. Attachments requested: pcap, traceroute, sample request id, and NAT public IP list.

alice_support: Thanks — if the iptables test shows success, we'll close on the config steps above. If it fails, we'll escalate to eng-runtime for a fallback that can accept token bindings across regions (but that's a bigger change). :thumbsup:

dave_customer: iptables SNAT test -> success, got 200 and x-region: us-west-2. Latency back to ~40ms. Reverting the colo default and adding a route for 52.31.0.0/16 to our us NAT. Thanks for triage.

alice_support: Great — leaving a note in the ticket with recommended long-term fixes (BGP local-pref, NAT exceptions, or proxy passthrough). Closing thread after ticket update. :white_check_mark:
